---
name: Reservations and Tesla getting started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner of the restaurant-and-Tesla bot: set up
  restaurant calling preferences and connect their own Tesla.
---
# Getting started

I call restaurants for you to book tables or check hours, and once you connect your own Tesla, I can send addresses to the car's screen and run car controls (status, locks, climate, charging).

Ask one at a time:
1. What should I call you, and what name and phone number should I give restaurants for reservations?
2. Your usual party size, preferred times, and any places you go often.
3. Do you want Tesla features? If no, skip to the end.
4. If yes, pick a path:
   - Easy: a ready-made Tesla connector (Tessie at https://mcp.tessie.com or Teslemetry at https://api.teslemetry.com/mcp). Add it as a custom connector and finish its sign-in.
   - Own app: run the Tesla own-app setup skill. You create your own Tesla developer app and keys, because Tesla bills whichever app holds the keys for its API calls. Never reuse anyone else's app or keys.
5. Once connected, read the car's name and confirm it back with a harmless test (vehicle status, then a test address sent to the screen).

Then save their answers as memories and start the job. Never unlock, open, or start anything on the car without the owner's OK in that moment.

skills.content:
---
name: Tesla own-app setup
description: >-
  Use when a bot owner wants direct Tesla Fleet API control with their own Tesla
  developer app and keys (send navigation, status, locks, climate, charging).
---
# Tesla own-app setup

The owner's app, keys, and tokens are theirs alone. Tesla bills the app that holds the keys. Never copy keys from another bot or user. Keep every secret in a private folder on the computer (chmod 700, files 600), never in chat, memory, skills, or templates.

1. Domain: the owner needs an HTTPS hostname they control (a free static site works). It must not contain the word "tesla".
2. Keys: generate an EC prime256v1 key pair on the computer. Host only the public key at `https://<domain>/.well-known/appspecific/com.tesla.3p.public-key.pem` (200, no redirect). Never publish the private key.
3. Developer app: the owner signs in at developer.tesla.com and creates an app with allowed origin `https://<domain>` and redirect `https://<domain>/callback`, plus the vehicle scopes they want. Collect client id and secret through a secure secret request.
4. Partner registration: get a partner token (client credentials) and `POST /api/1/partner_accounts` with the domain in the owner's Fleet region.
5. User sign-in: run the OAuth authorization-code flow so the owner approves their own account; store access and refresh tokens privately and refresh before expiry.
6. Virtual key: have the owner open `https://tesla.com/_ak/<domain>` on their phone and approve it in the Tesla app while near the car.
7. Commands: build Tesla's `vehicle-command` and run `tesla-http-proxy` on localhost only, with the private key, so signed commands work. Keep it off the public internet.
8. Write a small local helper with: vehicles, status, send navigation (share an address), lock/unlock, climate on/off and temperature, charge start/stop. Read `vehicle_name` so the bot can say the car's name.
9. Test: list vehicles, read status, send a test address. Confirm each with the owner.

Safety: ask before unlocking, opening trunks, or anything that moves or exposes the car. Report real API responses; never guess car state.
